title: Whose smoke was it in 1850?
hook: Several countries burned coal by 1850. How was the world's CO2 split between them?

doesNotKnow: how concentrated early fossil-fuel emissions were in one country
that a share can fall while the total rises

misconception: Early industrial emissions were spread across the industrial countries.
objective: The learner can say that in 1850 Britain produced about 62% of the world's fossil-fuel CO2, that its share fell to about 21% by 1900 while its own tonnes rose (122 to 420 Mt) and the world's grew about 10 times, and that a falling share can hide a rising total.

claims.text: Fossil-fuel CO2 in 1850: United Kingdom 122.3 Mt of a world 196.8 Mt, so Britain made 62% (stage label 'Britain 62%' at 1850; readout 'Britain, 1850 62%'; reveal 'In 1850 Britain produced 62% of the world's fossil-fuel CO2').
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, owid-co2-data.csv, column co2 (million tonnes), rows United Kingdom and World, year 1850; share is a derivation, history-cycle1-check.mjs section 9 ('1850 share'). 'Britain' on the stage is OWID's 'United Kingdom' entity. Brief claims 1-2.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Re-derived in my own node script from the pinned file (history-data.mjs pins all hold; sha256 re-checked) and compared with the copied array in Demo.tsx (identical). co2: UK 1850 122.350, World 196.848 Mt; 62.15%, shown 62%. In 1850 World co2 = coal_co2 (196.848), so 'fossil-fuel CO2' is exact here. OWID codebook (opened): co2 = 'Annual total emissions of carbon dioxide (CO2), excluding land-use change, measured in million tonnes'.

claims.text: Shares at the four preset years (stage end labels): 1800 Britain 96%, US 1%, Germany 2%, France 0%, others 1%; 1850 Britain 62%, US 10%, Germany 8%, France 10%, others 10%; 1900 Britain 21%, US 34%, Germany 17%, France 7%, others 22%; 1950 Britain 8%, US 43%, Germany 9%, France 3%, others 37%.
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, column co2, rows World, United Kingdom, United States, Germany, France, 1750-1950, rounded to 0.1 Mt in Demo.tsx; share = country / World; 'Others' = World minus the four. A country with no row is drawn as zero (US before 1800, Germany before 1792, France before 1802). UK 1800 95.6%, 1900 21.4%, 1950 8.4% and the US largest in 1900 (33.8%) match history-cycle1-check.mjs section 9. Brief claim 2.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): RAW in Demo.tsx = file co2 rounded to 0.1 Mt for all 5 entities, 1750-1950 (201 values each, 0 mismatches; missing rows drawn as 0, first rows US 1800, Germany 1792, France 1802). Shares: 1800 95.6/0.8/2.4/0/1.3; 1850 62.2/10.1/7.7/10.0/10.1; 1900 21.4/33.8/16.6/6.6/21.5; 1950 8.4/42.9/8.6/3.4/36.7. All round to the stage labels.

claims.text: By 1900 Britain's share had fallen to 21% while its own emissions rose from 122 to 420 Mt (readout 'Britain, 1900 21%'; tonnes view; reveal 'By 1900 its share had fallen to 21%' and 'A falling share can hide a rising total').
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, United Kingdom 1850 122.35, 1900 419.74 Mt; World 1900 1,962.9 Mt; 419.7 / 1,962.9 = 21.4%. history-cycle1-check.mjs section 9 ('1800 and 1900', 'tonnes rise while share falls').

claims.text: World fossil-fuel CO2 grew about 10 times from 1850 to 1900 (readout '1850 to 1900: World ×10'; reveal 'world emissions had grown 10 times').
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, World 1850 196.8 Mt, 1900 1,962.9 Mt: ×9.97, rounded to 10. history-cycle1-check.mjs section 9 ('world 1850 -> 1900 x10').

claims.text: The share fell as the United States, Germany and others burned more coal (reveal).
claims.source: history-data.mjs: co2, columns co2 and coal_co2: United States 19.8 -> 664.1 Mt (coal 626.5 in 1900), Germany 15.1 -> 326.8 Mt (coal 323.7), World coal 1,882.6 of 1,962.9 Mt in 1900 (96%). 'Burned more coal' is read from coal_co2, the CO2 the file attributes to coal; it is not a claim about why.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): US 19.793 -> 664.132 (coal 626.544), Germany 15.14 -> 326.759 (coal 323.729), World coal 1882.645 of 1962.884 in 1900. Read from coal_co2 as stated.

claims.text: Where it stops: these figures are rebuilt from records of coal and other fuels, and early years are the roughest (reveal). HELD: the one held source sentence. Fallback if not checkable: 'Where it stops: early years are the roughest estimates'.
claims.source: OWID co2-data README and the Global Carbon Project / CDIAC methods it cites (reachable from this host at raw.githubusercontent.com/owid/co2-data; not opened for this sentence). Brief claim 3, held.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Held. The brief's fallback ('early years are the roughest estimates') is exactly the unsourced half, so do not use it. recall.question: One town makes 9 of 10 bicycles in a region. Fifty years later it makes twice as many, but the region makes ten times as many. Its share?
recall.why: 18 of 100 is 18%: the town's output doubled, but the total grew ten times, so its share fell to a fifth. A falling share can hide a rising total.
